t: Foreign Service; b. July 31, 1891, Turkey; n. American; s. James D. Langdon, businessman. Career: Japanese lang. officer, Japan 1914-16; Vice-Cons. or Cons. in Japan, China and Canada since 1920. Present post: Amer. Cons. at Mukden. Address: American Consulate-General, Mukden, Manchoukuo.

a: Appendix I: Who's Who in Manchoukuo
t: (李紹庚) Diplomat; b. 1896, Shenyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov.; s. Li Yungwoo. Career: grad. Russian Com. Sch. 1920; Sino-Russian Law & Political Univ. Harbin; Chief Seer. Harbin Municipal Administration Bur.; Vice-Dir. same; Adv. to North Manchuria Ry. Administration Office, Fengtien Prov.; Cons.-Gen. at Vladivostok; Dir. Educ. Administration Bur. Harbin 1927; Dir. N. M. Ry. Administration Bur.; Chief-Dir. N. M. Ry. 1932-35. Minister of Communications, 1935-1940. Present post: Ambassador to Japan since 1940. Address: Manchoukuo Embassy, Tokyo.

t: (李文龍) Lieut.-Gen.; b. 1892 Lishu-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Mil. Coll. Fengtien; Comdr. 11th Reg. 16th Div. 1932; Comdr. 11th Inf. Reg. 4th Brig. Kirin Garrison 1933; Chief Staff 4th Mil. Dist.; Mil. Attache Embassy Tokyo 1937; Comdr. River Fleet since 1941. Address: Harbin.

a: Appendix I: Who's Who in Manchoukuo
t: (廖弼宸) Lt.-Gen., b. 1894, Suichung-hsien, Chinchow Prov. Career: grad. Infantry course of Paoting Military Acad.; Comdr. Liaoning Inf. 2nd Brig.; upon establishment of Manchoukuo apptd. Comdr. Yalu River Dist. Defense Hdqrs. in Fengtien Prov.; Comdr. Combined 1st Brig. of Fengtien Defense Army; Lt.-Gen. since 1934; Comdr. Fengtien Defence Hdqrs.; Comdr. Antung Defense Hdqrs. 1939. Present post: attached Dept. of Public Peace. Address: Public Peace Dept. Hsinking.

General Monopoly Bureau, Dept. of Economics, Hsinking.

t: (呂作新) Official; b. 1896 Chinchow Prov. Career: grad. Brewery Course, Osaka Engrg. Coll. 1926; Instructor Fengtien Prov. Police Sch. and Arsenal Sch.; Leader Autonomous Dept. Fengtien 1931; Commr. a: Appendix I: Who's Who in Manchoukuo
t: (盧元善) Official; b. 1888, Chinchow Prov. Career: educated in Japan; Dir. Shangcheng-chen-Yuke Elec. Co.; Staff Track Maintenance Sect. Szetao Ry. Bur.; entered Manchoukuo Govt. service upon its foundation; Secr. Defence Dept. 1932; Chief Ind. Dept. Lungkiang Prov. 1932; Chief Civil Affairs and Education Depts. of same; Dir. Gen. a: Appendix I: Who's Who in Manchoukuo
t: (廉隅) Diplomat; b. 1886 Wuhsi-hsien, Kiensu, China. Career: grad. LL.B. Law Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1907; passed students Abroad Examination and decorated with Chinshi by the Imperial Court of Ching Dynasty, 1907. Mem. Constitutional Bur.; Lecturer, Law Coll. and Fin. Coll.; Asst. Supt. of Students Abroad Exam. 1908; Chancellor, Mini. of Foreign Aff.; Judge, Supreme Court, 1909-1911; Chief Judge and Pres.-in-charge, Supreme Court, 1912; Pres. High Court of Chekiang, 1913; Pres. High Court of Chili and Honan, 1914-1920; Counsellor Secr. of State; Higher Adviser, Chili Prov. Gov. 1921-1923; Adviser, Shuh-jun Government of Gen. Juan-chi-zu; Councillor, National Assembly Prep. Bur.; Adv. Secr. of State; Secr. Min. of Finance; Asst. Debts Dept. of Min. of Fin. 1924-26. Practiced Law at Tientsin since 1927; Vice-Min. Foreign Aff. 1938; Foreign Min. 1939; Min. Ind. Ministry, Aug. 1939; Spec. Envoy of Ind. to Japan, March 1940; Kan-Char-Shi (Censorship) of Censorial Yuan Oct. 1940. Present post: Ambassador to Manchoukuo, since 1941. Address: Chinese Embassy, Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

a: Appendix I: Who's Who in Manchoukuo
t: (呂榮寰) Ambassador; b. 1890, Fushun, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Kiangsu Law Coll.; Vice-Pres. Mukden Assembly; sent to Washington Conf. as Repr. Three Eastern prov. 1923; went to Russia 1923; Chairman Soviet-Chinese Conf. & Mukden-Societ Conf.; Pres. Chinese Eastern Ry. 1924; Gov. Chinese Eastern Ry. 1927-29; Mayor of Harbin & Gov. North-Manchuria Special Dist. 1932-34; Pinkiang Prov. Dec. 1934-May 1935; Civil Affairs Min. 1935-37; Finance Min. May 1937; Minister of Industry until Dec. 1940. Present post: Ambassador to Nanking since Jan. 1941. Address: Manchoukuo Embassy, Nanking.
